title: The University of Verna
subtitle: Federation of colleges, keeper of copies
summary: A federation of colleges and archives that learned knowledge can disappear: Gate studies and its Laboratories in Endros, archival redundancy, provenance, restricted research and independence from patrons.
content:
> *"No library should be allowed to die only once."*
> — a saying among Vernan archivists

The **University of Verna** is one of the great scholarly institutions of the world, and one of the leading centres for the study of the Gates. It is also, Vernans will point out, a *Vernan* institution: the colleges of a small republic, transformed by the scholars who fled the [[silencing-of-the-schools|Silencing of the Schools]] into something far larger than either could have built alone. Its history is told in [[verna-and-the-university|Verna and the University]].

The University's deepest lesson comes from that history, and every member of it learns it early: **knowledge can disappear.** Libraries burn. Texts are seized. Schools are scattered. Almost everything distinctive about how the University works is a response to that fact.

## A Federation, Not a Campus

The University is not one campus or one school. It is better understood as a **federation** of colleges, faculties, laboratories, archives, hospitals, observatories and specialist institutes. That structure reflects how it grew: the many scholarly traditions that arrived in Verna were absorbed rather than flattened into a single institution, and many of them still keep their own character.

Among its best-known fields are **mathematics**, **medicine**, **astronomy**, **natural philosophy**, **archaeology**, **languages**, **engineering theory**, **historiography** and, increasingly, **Gate studies**. Every ordinary subject of a great university is taught somewhere within it as well. How the University is governed, and what its formal academic ranks are, are not set down here.

## Gate Studies and Endros

The University has become one of the world's leading institutions for the study of **Gates**, **artifacts**, **recovered materials**, the **[[why-we-call-them-the-valeoran-ruins|Valeoran Ruins]]**, **anomalous physical laws** and early **artificery**. Its presence in Endros is correspondingly large.

In Endros it runs the **University of Verna Laboratories**, which carry out archaeology, Gate studies, artifact analysis and experimental work. They appear among the Outpost's Research facilities on the [Outpost Sheet](outpost.html). University staff in Endros include researchers, archaeologists, historians, engineers, natural philosophers, physicians and field specialists.

The University works closely with the **Gate Evaluation Committee**, which evaluates newly discovered Gates, maintains their classifications and records, and recommends procedures for exploration and containment. The Committee is part of Endros's wider research infrastructure. It is not simply an arm of the University, though the two are rarely far apart.

The University also **sponsors Expeditioners**. It expects them to carry out research, submit samples, document what they find, publish and help University staff. In return they receive **Institutional Access**: once between expeditions, **+1 Progress** on a Research Project Action the University could plausibly help with. See the [University of Verna](game.html#post-faction-university-of-verna) Recruitment Faction rule.

> **In the University's receiving room in Endros, the day after a crew returned**
>
> The researcher had her notebook open before the Expeditioner sat down. "I'll need the samples, any sketches you made, the exact location, and the environmental conditions. Temperature, light, ground, anything you noticed."
>
> "It tried to eat me."
>
> "Yes." She wrote that down. "At what distance?"

## Archival Redundancy

Because knowledge can disappear, the University deliberately avoids **single points of failure**. Important materials are **copied**, **catalogued in more than one collection**, **stored in separate buildings** and **shared with trusted institutions**. A unique manuscript should not remain the only copy if another can reasonably be made.

Outsiders sometimes mistake this for bureaucracy. It is historical trauma turned into institutional policy, and Vernan archivists take it very seriously indeed.

> **In the reading room of a college library**
>
> "The exhibition opens on the first," said the visiting curator. "We had very much hoped to show the manuscript."
>
> "You will be able to," said the archivist, "as soon as the copy is finished."
>
> "When will that be?"
>
> "When it is finished." She did not look up from her ledger. "Until there are two of it, there is only one of it. And I have read about what happens to things there is only one of."

## Provenance

The University cares intensely about **provenance**: where a document or object came from, who has handled it, whether it is original, whether it has been altered, and how reliable its chain of custody is. In Gate research this matters enormously. A spectacular claim that cannot show where it came from is treated with great caution, however exciting it sounds, and University scholars are known for asking *"Where did this come from?"* before *"What does it do?"*

## Restricted Research

Verna does **not** believe that all knowledge should be kept secret. It also does **not** believe that everything should be published immediately. The University's position sits between the two: knowledge must be preserved and studied, but some dangerous information may need **controlled access**.

Restricted material may include unstable Gate phenomena, dangerous artifacts, procedures that could be catastrophically reproduced, and incomplete research likely to be misunderstood. How material is restricted, and who approves it, is not set down here. This is the single largest source of friction between the University and Vesperian scholars, and the Open Archive Incident (see [[the-vesper-republic|The Vesper Republic]]) is cited by both sides.

> **A Vesperian visitor and a Vernan professor, after a closed seminar**
>
> "If the discovery is true, why hide it?"
>
> "We are not hiding the truth," said the professor. "Anyone may read that the phenomenon exists, what we observed and what we believe it means. That is published."
>
> "Then what isn't?"
>
> "The procedure for reproducing it." He closed his folder. "We are not restricting the truth. We are restricting the instructions."

## How Vernans Publish

Vernan academic culture prefers **evidence**, **review**, **documentation**, **cautious claims** and **explicit uncertainty**. Researchers are trained to separate what was **observed** from how it is **interpreted**, what is **hypothesis** and what is mere **speculation**, and to say which is which. *"The evidence does not currently support that conclusion"* is heard in every faculty, and is not meant unkindly.

## Independence

The University resists being fully controlled by **governments**, **wealthy patrons** or **commercial institutions**. It does not refuse funding. It is deeply suspicious of funding that comes with authority over its **conclusions**, its **archives**, its **publications** or **who may see them**. That principle, too, grew out of its history: the last time a state decided which books could be read, Verna received the refugees.

> **In the director's office of a University library**
>
> The donor had given generously for many years, and said so.
>
> "I am not asking for anything unreasonable. A key to the restricted reading room, so that I may consult the collection at my convenience."
>
> "The collection is open to you on exactly the same terms as to every other reader," said the librarian. "Apply to the committee, state your purpose, and you will very likely be approved."
>
> "And if I were to withdraw my support?"
>
> "Then the library would be poorer, and I would be very sorry." She folded her hands. "And the reading room would still be open to you on exactly the same terms as to every other reader."

## Students, Colours and Ceremonies

Students are part of the University's identity, not background to it. They are intellectually competitive, socially organised, attached to their colleges and faculties, and proud of academic tradition.

Faculties and colleges have **distinct colours**, worn on formal robes and on ribbons, scarves, pins and trim. Which colour belongs to which faculty is not fixed in this entry. The University also has formal **ceremonies**: matriculation, graduation, faculty processions, public lectures, the presentation of faculty colours, and declarations of scholarly responsibility. Their exact form and wording are not recorded here.

## The University and the Powers

The University's relationships mirror Verna's (see [[verna-and-the-university|Verna and the University]]): close and argumentative with **Vesper**; cooperative but guarded with **Aurelia**, whose funding it values and whose priorities it resists; methodologically at odds and mutually useful with the **Vardic Holds**; respectful and politely curious with **Tianzhao**, whose archives, including those of the Festival of Returning Names, it would dearly like to see more of; and deliberately distant with **Kharad**, though Kharadi students are welcome.

In Endros, its most constant partner is **Nowhere Expeditions**, the company that brings so many Expeditioners to the Outpost. They cooperate extensively and disagree regularly, because they want different things. Nowhere Expeditions cares about getting people to Endros, keeping expeditions running, logistics and practical results. The University cares about documentation, preservation, samples, controlled study, publication and research ethics. Both are usually being reasonable.

> **At a worksite near the Ruins**
>
> "The artifact is in the middle of the access road," said the Nowhere Expeditions foreman. "Three crews are waiting to get past. We need it moved today."
>
> "And we need three more days," said the University archaeologist, "to document the soil underneath it."
>
> "The soil?"
>
> "Nobody has ever recorded what is under one of these. If you lift it now, nobody ever will."
>
> They looked at each other. Then the foreman sighed and went to find a longer way round.
